newsitem.title: EGYPT: Palestinian refugees plan sit-in on road to Libya.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian refugees plan sit-in on road to Libya.

text.p: Palestinian refugees deported by Libya last year said on Thursday they would hold a sit-in on the road that crosses the Egyptian-Libyan border to protest against Israeli practices.

The refugees plan to hold the four-hour sit-in on Friday morning to express their "support of fellow Palestinians in the occupied land against (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu's provocations against them," a camp resident said.
They were also protesting against "Netanyahu's failure to complete the peace process," he added.
Peace talks with the Palestinians stalled after Netanyahu's far-right government took power in June.
The Palestinian deportees postponed the sit-in, planned for Thursday, after "the Egyptian security authorities convinced them not to close the road," the camp resident added.
Some 220 refugees remain at the border camp, expelled by Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi more than a year ago to expose what he sees as a hollow peace deal between Israel and their leaders.
The refugees were reported last week to have closed the road for 24 hours after a dispute between some of them and Libyan customs officers.

Diplomats in Cairo have said there were high-level contacts between Egypt, Libya, the Arab League and United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees that might allow the Palestinians to leave the camp soon. Aid workers have described the camp as a rubbish dump unfit for human habitation.
Egypt has so far refused to let in the Palestinians unless they have travel documents to another country, but has made exceptions for a few serious medical cases.
